Tuition and University fees Expand all sections

How do I know if I am a new (commencing) or continuing (returning) student?

Different fee groups apply for new (commencing) and continuing (returning) students in each year. Please see definition below, to be read in conjunction with the Fee Group definitions:

New (Commencing) students:

Never enrolled into any program at RMIT Vietnam; or

Return after a period of no enrolment; or

EU: returning after a gap of 6 months or more

Academic program: 1 semester gap without a valid enrolment status (Enrolled, LOA) except for intake unavailability reason

Completed a Bachelor, Master, or PhD program and enrol in another program; or

Completed a Foundation Studies program and articulate to another program; or

Completed an English language program and enrol in another program; or

For example:

Completed Teen program and enrol in EU program; or

Completed a UniStart Academic or Graduate Certificate without a package offer, and enrol in another program

Not otherwise classified as a continuing (returning) student.

Continuing (Returning) students:

Have remained continuously enrolled or are on an approved LOA; or

Transferring to another program without completing the previous program while remain continuous enrolment or on an approved LOA; or

Completed UniStart Academic or Graduate Certificate as part of a package offer, and articulate to another program without any semester gap or with a semester gap due to intake unavailability.

My tuition fee has increased this semester. Why?

Annual fee adjustments have been applied in line with the Consumer Price Index and changes in operating costs, enabling us to continue to improve our quality.

When will I receive my tuition debit note for the new semester?

A debit note is emailed to students on Friday before the new semester starts.

If there are any enrolment changes, there are two ways to check updated tuition fees

View your Financial Account via myRMIT on the day after enrolment changes

Received updated debit notes on every Wednesday in the semester

Do I get a receipt or confirmation of payment?

If you need to confirm payment, you can check via the Financial Account tile in myRMIT , or ask a Student Connect advisor; however, payments may take up to three days to clear.

When is the deadline for payment?

The Payment deadline for tuition fees is on Friday in Week 3 of each semester, except for Block courses and Intensive PostGrads courses as follows:

Block course: the deadline for payment is on Friday of the first week of the block course.

Intensive PostGrads course: the deadline for payment is on the day before the course's start date.

What happens if I miss the tuition payment deadline?

Failure to pay all fees and charges by the Payment Date may result in a student being withdrawn from all enrolled courses and placed on administrative Cancellation unless exceptional circumstances apply, and a timely application is lodged and approved.

The penalty will affect students whose have overdue amount is as follows:

Standard course: greater than or equal to 5 million VND

Block course and Intensive Postgrad course: greater than or equal to 1 million VND

The penalties for withdrawal will be determined based on the corresponding timeline of the courses.

You will receive an updated tuition fee debit note that reverses course fees. However, library and other fees will not be reversed.

Can I seek an extension of payment?

Extensions are permitted in specific circumstances. You can read more here .

How can I pay my tuition fees?

You can pay tuition fees via the Financial Account tile in myRMIT , or by bank transfer or by credit card. Visit this link for more details regarding payment methods.

My debit note/my outstanding balance has a negative number. What does it mean?

When a number is negative, for example -2,000,000 VND, it means that amount is in credit or being reversed from an earlier debit note or a waiver.

If your total balance is in credit, you may be eligible for a refund or re-credit; any amount in credit can be used to offset against future fees.

What is the deadline for adding/dropping courses without penalty?

By Friday in Week 4 to avoid incurring full fees.

By Friday in Week 8 to avoid avoid incurring full fees and academic penalty of NN grade (Fail).

Except for Block courses and Intensive PostGrads courses as follows:

Block course:

Drop by the Friday of Week 2 to avoid incurring full fees.

Drop by the Friday of Week 3 to avoid incurring full fees and academic penalties.

PostGrad intensive course:

Drop on the first intensive day to avoid incurring full fees.

Drop by the second intensive day to avoid incurring full fees and academic penalties.

What if I am placed on administrative Cancellation due to Unpaid Fee and would like to come back to study?

You are allowed to come back to study the following semester, subject to the terms and conditions outlined in the Student Fees and Charges Guide (PDF, 803KB, 65p). Any outstanding debt must be paid before the student can successfully re-apply for entry into RMIT Vietnam or another campus of RMIT University.

I am going to study at RMIT next semester; however I have to cancel my enrolment. Can I get a refund on my deposit?

The deposit of 20 million VND is generally non-refundable and will only be refunded if you are given a conditional offer but fail to meet the conditions of that offer, OR if the University cancels an intake into a program.

I have a credit in my RMIT account but I do not want to apply for a refund as I am continuing to study. Can I use my credit for future fees?

Yes. The amount you have will be kept in credit and deducted from future tuition fees.

I am enrolled in courses and have paid my tuition fees. However, due to my sickness, I cannot study this semester and the deadline of LOA submission has passed. Can I get a refund of my fee or a re-credit for a future semester?

You may qualify for a Remission of Debt. Contact Student Connect for instructions on how to submit a remission of debt form and supporting documents.

Do I have to pay a medical insurance fee?

The medical insurance fee is compulsory for both local and international students studying at RMIT Vietnam. Should students choose to arrange their own medical insurance, evidence of insurance must be provided at least 10 days before a semester starts. Students can apply for an insurance waiver via myRMIT .

More information can be found on the Health Insurance page.

How can I use online payment via Vietcombank-iB@NKING

Follow the instruction below for online payment via VCB-iB@NKING (only applied for VCB-iB@nking users):

Go to Vietcombank website here

Log in, select Payment, then Bill payment.

Select service, Tuition fee, Select service provider, RMIT Vietnam - HCM campus  or RMIT Vietnam - Hanoi campus.

Select fee type from the drop-down list, Fill in the payment amount, Fill in the Customer code (Student ID Number or Birth Date only if Student ID is not issued), Fill in Customer name (Student name) and Confirm.

Enter verification code → Confirm

Enter OTP (Sent via SMS to the phone number registering with the bank)

Confirm (successful transactions will be confirmed by SMS and email).

For Customer code:

Enter correctly the Student ID Number with the following format: Sxxxxxxx or Lxxxxxxx (x: number). If you don’t have Student ID Number yet, enter your birthdate with the following format: xxyyzzzz (xx: date; yy: month; zzzz: year).

For Customer name:

Enter full name of Student – NOT name of account owner if the account owner is not the student.

Cashless campus Expand all sections

Can I use any bankcard to complete a cashless transaction?

Yes, all cards and bank transfers are accepted.

Will I be charged any additional charges on top of the purchase price to cover a vendor fee?

No.

Can I use a QR code?

Yes, you can use QR codes that link to multiple e-wallets/banks.

How do I pay with a QR code?

You can use electric devices such as smartphone, tablet to scan the QR code that connects to an e-wallet application. Each vendor will choose to connect with different brands of e-wallet to provide customers with various choices that are available in their devices.

Can I use any e-wallet or is it specific to the vendor?

Each vendor may choose to connect with different brands of e-wallet.

I don’t have a bank account or a bank card, what should I do?

In SGS campus, student can buy a VietcomBank (VCB) Prepaid Debit Card at the cashier counter at Level 1, Building 2. This card is only offered to students who are ineligible to open a bank account and guests visiting campus.

Hanoi campus do not offer food and parking services.

The motorbike parking fees is just a few thousand dong, can I pay by cash?

You can choose to pay parking fees by cash or cashless methods upon your preference.

Will there be any options to purchase food with cash on campus after this new program commences?

You can choose to pay for food and drinks by cash or cashless methods upon your preference. Paying your tuition fees with cashless methods Expand all sections

How can I pay tuition fees now the campus is cashless? Methods Description MyRMIT Log in to myRMIT , and pay cashless via the Financial Account tile. Bank transfer

Internal and external bank transferring

POS machine (*)

(Accept all banks card and card’s types)

Saigon South: Banking staff will support to take payment at cashier counter in regular working day.

Hanoi: Banking staff will support to take payment at cashier counter in regular working day

Danang: Banking staff will support to take payment at the cashier during agreed days following to payment schedule of SEUP. RMIT’s cashier counter will close out of agreed days. Cash transaction

At any VCB branches offices or

At any other banks to make a cash deposit to VCB account. RMIT payment website Visit the RMIT payment website here .

Note: The minimum transaction amount allowed to be paid via RMIT website & myRMIT is 10,000 VND.

How can I get the payment receipt when I pay online?

Payment receipt will be sent to your email.

Note: The minimum transaction amount allowed to be paid via RMIT website & myRMIT is 10,000 VND.

I am an international student and do not have a local bank account in Vietnam yet. How can I pay the tuition fee?

You can make payment via the Financial Account tile in myRMIT , or by external bank transfer or international bank cards at POS machine.

If I forgot a bank card at home, what can I do?

You can pay your fees via the Financial Account tile in myRMIT . Alternatively, you can purchase a Gift Card at the cashier counter at Level 1, Building 2, SGS campus and then use it for your payment. Other information on cashless campus Expand all sections

What is the VCB gift card?

The VietcomBank (VCB) Gift Card is issued on SGS campus by VCB at the cashier counter: Level 1, Building 2. It is only offered to students who are ineligible to open a bank account or first-time visitors to campus.

I am only on campus as a visitor, do I still need to use a VCB Gift Card?

It is not required to have a Gift Card to use services if you already have other bank cards or use e-wallets.

How do I obtain a VCB Gift Card / where on campus in SGS, Hanoi and Danang can I purchase one?

The VCB Gift Card is only offered at Saigon South campus. It can be bought at our cashier counter located at Level 1, Building 2 from Monday to Friday during working hours (8am-12pm / 1-5pm).

The VCB gift card can be used to pay for food and drink and parking fees. Therefore, it only valid in SGS campus because RMIT does not offer these services in Hanoi and Danang campuses.

What happens if I have left over credit on my VCB Gift Card, can it be refunded to me?

The balance on this card is not eligible for cashback. The value of the card is VND 100,000 and you can use it in RMIT campuses in 3 years from the issuance date.

Will the VCB Gift card expire?

The card will expire 3 years from the issuance date.

I’ve lost my VCB gift card, what do I do?

The VCB Gift Card once assigned is your responsibility. RMIT and VCB are not responsible for the security or replacement of your card if lost.

How can I check the balance of the VCB Gift Card?

You can check the balance at the VCB cashier located on campus at Level 1, Building 2

Can I use Apple Pay/Momo/other e-wallets?

It varies. Please check with the vendors for e-wallet options.

If my bank card has an error, how can I pay a parking fee?

You will park your vehicle at a separate area and then buy a Vietcombank Gift Card at the cashier counter Level 1, Building 2, SGS campus. The parking fee will be paid when check-out. Besides that, you need to check with the issuer bank for an error and issue a new card if needed.

Who do I contact for queries?

Please send your queries to Student Connect Related links and downloads
